ranked_challengers.evidence_and_limitations: Second, beaten two lengths, on 2m hurdle debut at Ffos Las. Has jumping experience and scope to improve.
Won an Exeter bumper decisively. Still has to transfer to hurdles.
Fourth on hurdle debut over 2m at Worcester. Likely to improve with experience, though a longer trip may prove better.

records.analysis: Third, three lengths behind River Kwai, originally rank 2. Number-one rival and proven hurdler Oatsoeasy was withdrawn for unsuitable ground. River Kwai was also transferring from a bumper, so this supports the named opposition and gives limited support to a proven-hurdle-experience mechanism.

ranked_challengers.evidence_and_limitations: Dual chase winner back down to his last winning mark and into a 0–100 after a shorter-trip return at Hexham.
A point winner with scope to build on his Newcastle chasing debut. Improvement is still required.

records.analysis: Made the running and beat original rank 1 Flash Du Pistolet by 20 lengths. Original rank 2 Humble Jumble finished fifth. The jump from 86 to 92 did little to stop the lightly raced mare on her second chase start. The specific chase-rise case failed despite the strongest rival finishing second.

ranked_challengers.evidence_and_limitations: Won at Uttoxeter and both rivals won next time. Fell on his subsequent start and gives Klub De Reve 5 lb.
Point winner and Grade 2 hurdle runner-up. Has his own chase transfer upside but lacks Rules chase evidence.
Point winner receiving 14 lb from the favourite. Less accomplished over hurdles and also a Rules chase debutant.

records.analysis: Won by six lengths from original rank 1 Country Mile, with original rank 2 Masked Man third. Original rank 3 Hardly Surprising was withdrawn, so the expected depth was reduced. The favourite’s point-winning and Grade 2 hurdle form transferred on Rules chase debut. Country Mile’s experience did not offset the favourite’s upside.

ranked_challengers.evidence_and_limitations: Last year's winner, second over the same course and distance in March. Effective 11 st 10 lb after Jay Tidball's 5 lb claim. Pulled up on his 3m reappearance.
Course winner, back to his last winning mark after a recent Aintree run. Cheekpieces are refitted. The latest fourth was well beaten.

records.analysis: Official non-runner. Original ranks 1 and 2, Twinjets and Etalon, finished first and second, five lengths apart. The finishing order confirms the rivals were competitive in the reduced field. The favourite’s prospects, 9 lb rise and return from a break could not be tested. Bluey and Gemirande also did not run.

ranked_challengers.evidence_and_limitations: Won a 22-runner 6f Doncaster handicap and remains unbeaten in two all-weather starts.
Narrow second in a Dundalk Group 3 on all-weather debut. Has not consistently reproduced his peak form.

records.analysis: Fifth after leading and weakening late. Beckford’s Folly won on his first run in 209 days, with Montassib second. Neither was a frozen ranked challenger. Crestofdistinction and Ain’t Nobody were sixth and fourth. The result supports a broad opposition case only. It does not show the break or the Tapeta caused the defeat. Give proven class at equal weights a fuller assessment when a horse can run well fresh.

ranked_challengers.evidence_and_limitations: Second in a 6f Curragh maiden. Drops in grade and returns to a more suitable test after two 5f runs. First try at 7f.
Improved on her second start when sixth over 6f here and receives 5 lb. Needs another step forward at 7f.

records.analysis: Waysong passed the post first by a nose. The weighed-in result reversed the first two and placed Chicago Caray first. The paper lay therefore lost at the frozen 4.60. Original ranks 1 and 2 Rejoinder and Let Me Free were fourth and fifth. Chicago Caray's class drop nearly yielded a win on the track. The amendment determined settlement and gives limited evidence about the expected competition.

lessons: Require concrete evidence that a rival can beat the favourite’s likely improvement. A handicap rise or debut over fences is a question, and the favourite’s prior point win or scope to improve on chase start two can answer it.

Treat race settlement, winner identification and mechanism as separate observations. River Kwai was named but used the same bumper-to-hurdle route as the horse opposed. Beckford’s Folly was outside the frozen ranks.
Keep the Kap Ouest void out of the win-rate denominator. The two ranked rivals finishing first and second provides no test of Kap Ouest’s chance.
Record first observation times and downgrade only the specific opposition weakened by withdrawals. Keep original ranks, approved prices and theory eligibility frozen.
